cases.name: Arlis Kay Dykema Perry
cases.about:
She had recently moved to the Stanford University campus with her husband, who was a sophomore pre-med student. At the time of her murder, she had been working as a receptionist at a local law firm.

I just want people to know that she was really special, beautiful soul. She had a wonderful spirit for being 19. She was a fun-loving, smart, kind, compassionate, person who had a very strong faith and just a love for life.
— Jenny, Arlis’s best friend
cases.caseStatus: CODIS / DNA MATCH; COLD CASE SOLVED; SUSPECT DECEASED WHEN ID'D
cases.narrative:
He stabbed her in the head with an ice pick, causing penetrating injuries of the cranium.

He claimed to have found her in a church at Stanford University, where he worked as a security guard, at 5:45am, face-up with her hands across her chest. She had been brutally killed, with reports saying she was found with an ice-pick in her head and she had been sexually assaulted with a candlestick.

The Mercury News reported that an ice pick had been driven into the back of Perry’s skull, and said that “her body had been violated with church candles.”

cases.name: Janet Ann Taylor
cases.about:
She had attended Canada College in Redwood City until January 1974 and was working at Oceanside Inc., a maritime information firm in Palo Alto.

It was unimaginable. I mean she was a kind soul. She was really a giving person. You know, I can’t imagine anybody hurting her.
— Russell, Janet’s ex-boyfriend
cases.caseStatus: CODIS / DNA MATCH; CONVICTION; FORENSIC INVESTIGATIVE GENETIC GENEALOGY SOLVED
cases.narrative: On 3/25/1974, Ernesto Evangelia worked for the peninsula Creamery and was delivering milk to stores and as he passed the area of Manzanita on Sand Hill Road, he saw what he thought was debris on the side of the road. He decided to stop his truck get out and inspected the debris he saw on the side of the road. The debris that he saw on the side of the road was Janet. Janet was clothed but she didn't have any shoes on. Her feet were clean. They were not muddy, but it had been raining out all night. Her body was damp. Under her body, it was dry. Her clothes were torn, underwear was missing and had been stuffed down her throat. Her face was bruised. She had been beaten severely. She'd been strangled to death and left on the side of the road.

cases.name: Leslie Marie Perlov
cases.about:
She was a Stanford University graduate and aspiring law student.

Leslie was always brilliant and thoughtful and very quick. She always got straight A’s in school. She went through high school in three years. She went through college in three years. She got a scholarship at Stanford and she had applied to law schools and at the time of her death, she was waiting to see what school she would get into.
— Diane, Leslie’s sister
cases.caseStatus: CODIS / DNA MATCH; COLD CASE SOLVED; FORENSIC INVESTIGATIVE GENETIC GENEALOGY SOLVED
cases.narrative: On 2/16/1973, her body was found by members of the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office in an area west of Stanford that was commonly referred to as the Dish. Leslie was found naked from the waist down with her skirt pulled above her waist, her face was bruised, with her underwear used as a ligature around her neck, her pantyhose had been stuffed down her throat, and she died as a result of strangulation.

cases.name: Kristine Pedersen Fitzhugh
cases.about: Kristine was a music teacher at Addison Elementary in Palo Alto, CA.
cases.narrative: On 5/5/2000, her body was found during a welfare check after she failed to show up for work. He hit her on the back of the head 7 times and strangled her, then placed her body at the foot of the stairs in an attempt to stage her death as an accidental fall.
